name: RocksDB
model: Library for sorted byte-string keys and values: get, put, delete, range scans, column families, snapshots
engine_note: Log-structured merge tree: writes go to a WAL and memtable, flush to sorted SST files, background compaction merges them
consistency: One process; batches of writes (WriteBatch) are atomic; snapshots give consistent reads; optional optimistic or pessimistic transactions. WAL is on but not fsynced per write by default (sync=false), so a machine crash can lose the latest writes.
scaling: Single machine, single process. Bigger disks and more compaction threads; systems such as CockroachDB (via Pebble, a Go port), TiKV and Kafka Streams build sharding on top.
licence: Dual GPLv2 or Apache License 2.0 (your choice)
version_note: HISTORY.md on main already lists 11.9.0 (2026-08-14), 11.10.0 (2026-08-28) and 11.11.0 (2026-09-21), but those are not tagged on GitHub; 11.8.1 is the latest tagged release.
reach: Reach for it when you are building a storage system or need a fast, write-heavy local key-value store inside one process (state stores, indexes, queues).
avoid: Avoid when you want a database server with SQL, users and replication; you would be building those parts yourself, and tuning compaction takes skill.
escape: You need a write-optimised key-value engine inside your own program, not a server.
chat: Nothing directly; it may be the storage engine under a database or stream processor the chat app uses.
notes: Licence class set to permissive because Apache 2.0 can be chosen. Default WriteOptions.sync=false: writes reach the OS but are not fsynced, so a process crash keeps them but a power or OS crash can lose recent ones (per Basic-Operations wiki). Users of RocksDB as an engine (TiKV, Kafka Streams state stores) are general knowledge, not individually sourced here; CockroachDB moved to Pebble, its own Go LSM inspired by RocksDB. No Jepsen report (embedded library).
